title: My AI playtest bots said my first 4 waves were easy. 7 of my first 9 real players quit there
author: Al-Cohol0802
selftext:
I made Shadow Sweep, a small browser game where your shadow is the weapon. You walk around a lamp and whatever your shadow covers takes damage. Enemy shadows hurt you too.

Free in the browser (phone or desktop): [https://c2h5oh-game-lab.itch.io/shadow-sweep](https://c2h5oh-game-lab.itch.io/shadow-sweep)

I've been building it for 38 days with Claude Code (Opus). I make the design calls and Claude writes the code.

For difficulty, Claude wrote four simple bot players. They play every wave in a fixed-step simulation and report how much light each wave costs. All four said the first four waves cost 0 HP. Then 9 people from outside played, and 7 of them stopped somewhere in those first four waves, most at full health. So the bots were right that it was easy, they just can't tell me why people left. I merged two tutorial waves anyway, but nobody from outside has played since, so I don't know yet if it helped.

None of the art is an image file. The moths, the lamp, the town square and the menus are all drawn in code.

The clip is from another bot. It plays the live build with fake touch input, moving the joystick like a thumb would. It runs on a clock that steps one frame at a time, so the recording doesn't drop frames. I hid the HUD for it.

If you try it, I'd love to know where you would have stopped. That's the part my bots can't tell me.

comments.author: Fit_Eye_3564
comments.body: I think itd at a good level, but the one pink moth final boss is too strong that it stays at the center. Only way to cool it at thay point is to take damage from it I believe? Also joystick response dies a lot for me on my android. Really messed with my gameplay and make movement feel really terrible. Cute game tho
